title: schema-fence: decoder guardrail scenarios for streaming + tool-call interleaving
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Create a focused test suite and runbook for the ‘schema-fence’ behavior: how the constrained decoder enforces JSON/schema contracts during streaming responses, especially when tool/function calls or partial tokens are interleaved. This ticket drives additions to the test harness, defines deterministic scenarios for prefix-loss and sentinel insertion, and codifies expected rapid-recovery behavior and safety fallbacks across runtime variants.
goal: Reduce production regressions related to constrained decoding failure modes in streaming and tool-call interleavings; provide deterministic pass/fail criteria and an operator runbook for rollbacks and mitigations.
background: We continue to see edge failures where partial streaming outputs + tool-return fragments confuse the constrained decoder and cause schema violations or silent truncation. Existing suites cover full-stream JSONmode and simple toolcalls but lack dense interleaving scenarios (e.g., tool call emits JSON fragment, runtime injects sentinel mid-token, network reconnect with KV-cache mismatch). This work complements broader streaming schema efforts and will be used to gate runtime-1.22.
tasks: Define 12 deterministic scenarios that combine: short/long prefix, tool return mid-response, truncated token boundaries, KV-cache mismatch, and client reconnect.
Add new fixtures to the structured-output harness to replay recorded model outputs with injected tool-call events and partial tokens.
Implement comparator that validates schema conformance incrementally (per-chunk) and after finalization; flag both hard failures and acceptable relaxations.
Extend CI to run the suite against three runtime variants: optimized-kernel, quantized-INT8, and fallback-CPU, capturing token-level logs.
Author operator runbook with rollback steps, mitigation flags, and recommended model fallbacks (model-compat-v1/v2) for on-call.
Coordinate with SDK team to add a debug flag that records raw chunk frames and sentinel events for postmortem analysis.
Run canary in staging with traffic replay for 48 hours and collect pass/fail, latencies, and false-positive relaxations metrics.
test_matrix: Scenario A: Toolcall mid-stream with well-formed JSON fragment -> expect streaming enforcer merges and validates final schema
Scenario B: Toolcall mid-stream with malformed fragment (missing comma) -> expect decoder to apply sentinel injection and return structured error object per contract
Scenario C: Truncation at token boundary -> expect reassembly from prefix snapshot + deterministic recovery within 1 chunk
Scenario D: KV-cache mismatch after reconnect -> expect gating to fall back to non-batched mode and emit warning metric
Scenario E: Quantized runtime variant produces subtle tokenization drift -> expect schema-fence to detect deviation and route to compatible model-variant automatically
acceptance_criteria: All 12 scenarios implemented as CI tests and green across the three runtime variants
No more than 0.2% schema-violation rate in the 48h staging replay (target: 0%)
Operator runbook published and reviewed by SRE and PM (pgp signature or doc link in PR)
SDK debug flag available and documented in the console telemetry guide
Automated rollback policy triggers on two consecutive hard-schema failures in canary traffic
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spike completed. Reproduced failure mode with recorded model that emits '}]]' mid-chunk when tool returns nested object.
2026-02-18: Design review with Runtime and SDK teams. Decided to prefer sentinel-insert-and-continue over hard-abort for mixed toolcall scenarios to preserve latency SLOs.
2026-02-25: Added comparator prototype that validates per-chunk JSON parseability and tags 'soft-relax' vs 'hard-violation'.
2026-03-03: SRE requested additional observability: token-level origin tagging (model vs tool vs runtime). Implemented in harness.
2026-03-08: PR #9871 opened to add test scenarios and the canary orchestration manifest. CI currently failing on quantized-INT8 variant for Scenario E.
2026-03-10: Investigating quantized tokenization drift with Research. Next steps: add tokenizer-alignment shim and run new CI matrix.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict abort on first schema violation reduces downstream ambiguity but increases tail-latency and potential partial-commit visibility for clients. We adopted a two-tier response: soft-relax warnings plus a structured error object for unrecoverable cases.
We will not change public API surface for this ticket; SDK debug flag is opt-in for customers and internal use only.
If quantized variant continues to fail, plan B is to pin canary traffic to model-compat-v1 and schedule a runtime patch in runtime-1.22.1
